title: FTO check: Integrated Harness and Shoulder Module vs. harness patents
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. The one-piece Integrated Harness (belt + shoulders sewn) sits closer to vest-style ride harness patents than the Hip Belt alone.
objective: Compare the Integrated Harness and Shoulder Module design rules in concepts.md against the claims of US 11,975,679, EP 4 380 708, US 9,162,089 and any other vest/shoulder-harness patents found, and list design constraints.
acceptanceCriteria: Claim-by-claim comparison table for each patent
Concrete design constraints added to concepts.md as DRAFT
States clearly that it is not a legal opinion
Every factual claim has a cited, working source link; estimates are labelled as estimates
